item.title: Livelihood, education goals affect migration under climate change
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Climate-driven hazards can push many to leave their homes in search of a livelihood elsewhere, but aspirations for the future may change where they decide to migrate, according to a new study led by researchers at Penn State. At the same time, income losses due to climate shocks, or extreme weather events like floods or droughts, may constrain migration options for vulnerable populations.

item.title: Urban street trees lose much of their capacity to cool during droughts
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: The combination of heat waves and drought markedly reduces the capacity of street trees to cool the air in Mediterranean cities. The lack of soil moisture severely restricts plant transpiration, reducing the thermal relief provided by these trees during extreme heat events.

item.title: Antarctic rocks reveal a missing chapter of glacier history
item.description:
Waypoint is curating and commenting on third-party reporting. Original publisher: Phys.org.
Summary: Antarctica's glaciers were changing long before satellites, weather stations or cameras captured their transformations, and they left behind clues. Along Marguerite Bay on the western Antarctic Peninsula, ridges of rocks and debris mark former glacier margins. For decades, scientists lacked direct evidence about when many of these ridges formed.
